topic: ORAL Surveillance trial: cardiovascular safety of tofacitinib vs TNFi in RA
synopsis: ORAL Surveillance compared tofacitinib with TNF inhibitors in a cardiovascular-risk-enriched rheumatoid arthritis population. This open report of the primary findings gives a hazard ratio for major adverse cardiovascular events of 1.33 (95% CI 0.91 to 1.94) for tofacitinib versus TNF inhibitors. Non-inferiority was not met because the prespecified criterion required the upper 95% confidence limit to be no higher than 1.80. Incidence rates were 0.98 per 100 patient-years (95% CI 0.79 to 1.19) with tofacitinib and 0.73 (95% CI 0.52 to 1.01) with TNF inhibitors. The excess MACE risk was more pronounced at age 65 years or older than under 65. The same summary states that malignancies excluding non-melanoma skin cancer, and infections, were also higher with tofacitinib than with TNF inhibitors.

teachingPoints.claim: MACE HR for tofacitinib versus TNFi was 1.33 (95% CI 0.91 to 1.94), and non-inferiority was not met.
teachingPoints.sourceExcerpt: hazard ratio=1.33; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.91 to 1.94). The non-inferiority criterion was not met (upper limit of 95% CI was >1.80).

teachingPoints.claim: The MACE increase was more pronounced at age ≥65 than under 65.
teachingPoints.sourceExcerpt: The increased risk of MACE with tofacitinib versus TNFi was more pronounced in patients aged ≥65 years than in patients aged <65 years.

teachingPoints.claim: Malignancies excluding non-melanoma skin cancer, and infections, were also higher with tofacitinib.
teachingPoints.sourceExcerpt: Risk of malignancies (excluding non-melanoma skin cancer) and infections was also higher with tofacitinib versus TNFi in ORAL Surveillance.

uncertaintiesNotedInSource: The hazard-ratio confidence interval crosses 1; the trial failed its non-inferiority criterion rather than proving a precise excess in every subgroup.
